mentions.name: Tenuo
mentions.description: This project is a capability-based authorization model for AI agents in which authority is explicit, task-scoped, and attenuating, adapted for workflows where delegation happens dynamically mid-task. It lets permissions be scoped per task (e.g., read-only on a table or a cap of 3 VMs) instead of granting ambient authority over all tools, with sub-agents not inheriting full access by default. It is closest to Macaroons/Biscuit, and the early prototype has a Rust core, a Python SDK, and a LangChain integration.
mentions.problem: Once an AI agent is given tools it gains ambient authority over all of them, with no clean way to express task-scoped permissions; sub-agents spawned mid-execution inherit full access by default, and IAM keeps authority tied to the agent's identity even as intent shifts during execution.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm exploring a capability-based model instead: authority is explicit, task-scoped, and attenuating. Closest to Macaroons/Biscuit, but adapted for workflows where delegation happens dynamically mid-task.

Early prototype (Rust core, Python SDK, LangChain integration), still thinking it through. Notes here: https://niyikiza.com/posts/capability-delegation/
